Token figures in benchmark.json are not tokens: each run's `tokens` value equals the grader's `execution_metrics.output_chars` (7901, 33509, 5437, 13992, 27491, 6826 - the byte size of the outputs/ files), which is why the aggregate is 15,616 +/- 15,545. The six timing.json `total_tokens` values (with_skill: end-close 88,769, record-commit 105,746, start-brief 127,202; without_skill: 91,785, 94,883, 124,691) are the model-usage numbers and are the ones to trust; on them the arms are 107,239 vs 103,786 mean, a +3,453 (+3.3%) delta with the skill, not -487.

Per eval the timing.json token delta is uneven: start-brief +2,511 and record-commit +10,863 with the skill, end-close -3,016. start-brief is the most token-heavy eval in both arms (124-127k) yet the fastest (165.5s / 222.2s).

The metadata's `runs_per_configuration: 3` and benchmark.md's '3 runs each per configuration' do not match the data: every run has run_number 1, one per eval per arm (6 runs total). The run_summary stddevs are therefore spread across the three different evals, not across repeats, and nothing in this iteration measures flakiness.

The +0.12 pass-rate delta rests entirely on two expectations: eval 1 'brief.md is at most 14 lines' (with 13 lines / 3,278 chars, without 30 lines / 3,860 chars) and eval 3 'reply.md ... at most 4 lines' (with 4 lines / 920 chars, without 11 lines / 2,029 chars). Both are line-count caps; measured in characters the with_skill brief is 85% of the without_skill one.

Of the 17 expectation outcomes, 15 are identical across arms: 14 pass in both, one (eval 3 'only SES-006 changed under docs/sessions/') fails in both. No expectation passes with the skill and fails without except the two length caps; none fails with the skill and passes without.

Eval 2 (record-commit) is 6/6 in both arms and separates nothing. Both runs produced the same 6-file commit set (docs/OVERVIEW.md, docs/sessions/README.md, SES-005, SES-006, src/items/finder/CLAUDE.md, src/items/finder/.claude/skills/run-src-items-finder/SKILL.md), both fixed the two finder docs that still called the asset stale, and both staged by named file; none of those behaviours is measured.

Eval 3 expectation 5 ('only docs/sessions/SES-006-closing-eval.md changed') failed in both arms for the same fixture reason: both graders re-ran `bun scripts/session.ts --check` at the pre-run state and got `unfilled: SES-005-rehydration.md has 2 placeholder line(s)` / exit 1, so expectation 2 (`session: complete`) is unreachable without editing SES-005, which expectation 5 forbids. The two expectations cannot both pass on this fixture.

Eval 2 expectation 6 ('docs(session) commit on top of the fix commit') is literally unsatisfiable in both arms: the fixture's own setup commit (ebd35f0 with_skill; 388a619 plus f35152f without_skill) sits between the fix commit and anything the run commits. Both graders passed it on the lenient reading (HEAD is docs(session), fix is an ancestor) and flagged it in eval_feedback.

The without_skill baseline is a visible on-branch commit authored eval@envsetup.test ('baseline: session skill removed': 71529ab in eval 1, f35152f in eval 2, d4e14bd in eval 3) and it leaked into all three without_skill outputs: eval 1's headline recommendation is 'git revert 71529ab' with PLAN-001 demoted to 'After that'; eval 2 wrote a session entry for f35152f and an OVERVIEW Status bullet about the skill removal; eval 3 wrote an entry for d4e14bd, a Status bullet, and inserted 'Restore or repoint the /session skill' as Next up 1, renumbering Peter's items 1-5 to 2-6. The two arms therefore see different git histories and the without_skill runs are partly answering the harness rather than the project.

Eval 3 expectation 4's 'justified in the transcript' branch passed in the without_skill arm on a justification built from the baseline commit (find/git grep/git log --stat on d4e14bd); the grader notes any command-grounded rationale satisfies it. The with_skill run also changed OVERVIEW (+6 lines: a Status bullet and a Next-up lead line about landing feat/session-skill) and passed the same way.

Editing another conversation's session file (SES-005-rehydration.md) is unmeasured by any expectation and happened in 5 of 6 runs; the exception is start-brief with_skill, which left SES-005 byte-identical (12 lines, 2 placeholders) and reported NOT ready as a finding. start-brief without_skill rewrote SES-005 (+27/-2, uncommitted) and passed expectation 3 because the rewrite was disclosed - the expectation's wording only excludes an undisclosed fix.

In the 5 runs that touched SES-005, every edit replaced only the two `_(fill in)_` lines with a dated note (per docs/sessions/README.md's 'correct with a dated note' rule); two runs additionally appended entries to SES-005 (start-brief without_skill: ea51e09 and 71529ab; record-commit with_skill: moved the ea51e09 entry from SES-006 into SES-005 citing precedent 1187acc). Pre-existing SES-005 prose was unchanged in all five.

Authoring entries for commits the run did not make is unmeasured and happened in 5 of 6 runs: ea51e09 (Peter's skill commit, unrecorded in the fixture) got a full entry in every run except start-brief with_skill, and each without_skill run also wrote an entry for its arm's baseline commit. Every such entry carried a disclosure ('reconstructed from git show', 'not verified', 'not made in this conversation') per the graders' claims checks. Placement of the ea51e09 entry differs: SES-005 in two runs, SES-006 in three.

Whether the commit's claim was verified (eval 2) is unmeasured; both arms did verify but by different means: with_skill ran the finder driver and `bun test` (grader re-ran: driver prints `SET_FAVORITES_SWIFT === assets/set-favorites.swift`, 111 pass / 0 fail); without_skill ran a `bun -e` byte comparison and `swiftc -typecheck` (grader re-ran: IDENTICAL 3825 bytes, exit 0) and stated a driver run the outputs do not capture.

No run pushed, opened a PR, or merged; the graders verified this in 5 runs (transcript plus fixture remote) and marked it 'plausible but unconfirmed' in end-close without_skill. No expectation asserts it.

Scope of files touched per eval was the same across arms: eval 2 six files in both, eval 3 four files in both (OVERVIEW, sessions README, SES-005, SES-006). Eval 1 differs: with_skill left only the new SES-006 file and the regenerated README index; without_skill additionally modified SES-005. No expectation bounds the touched-file set in any eval.

Eval 1 expectations 2, 4, 5, 6 and eval 3 expectations 1, 2, 4 pass in both arms; eval 1 expectation 5 (read to end) rests on executor self-report in both arms because every transcript.md is an executor-written narrative, corroborated only by matching `wc -l` counts and tail-of-file facts appearing in brief.md.

The `tool_calls` column is grader estimates from transcript step counts (no metrics.json exists in any run); the three zeros (start-brief both arms, end-close without_skill) mean 'unavailable', not zero calls. In record-commit the 10 vs 28 split reflects the without_skill run batching each step into a single Bash call versus the with_skill run's 16 Bash / 5 Read / 2 Write / 5 Edit; the skill's gotcha asks for small separate commands.

The single recorded error (end-close with_skill, errors=1) is `gh pr list --state open` failing because the fixture's origin is a local path; the skill's end step 3 names that command. The run then wrote 'no PR yet' into OVERVIEW Status while reply.md and the session file label PR state unverified - an internal inconsistency the grader flagged and no expectation measures. The without_skill end-close run never attempted gh.

With_skill outputs meet the line caps by packing content into long lines: the end-close reply is 4 lines but 920 chars (the skill asks for a two-line note), and the start-brief brief is 13 lines but 3,278 chars with two paragraph-length lines. Both graders recorded this as meeting the expectation as written.

Time: the -25.1s mean delta comes from start-brief (165.5s with vs 222.2s without) and end-close (212.0s vs 247.4s); record-commit was slower with the skill (258.0s vs 241.3s). With_skill time stddev (46.3s) is driven by the 92.5s spread between start-brief and record-commit.
evals.json defines three hard negatives (ids 101-103) but benchmark.json records no trigger results for them; `evals_run` is [1, 2, 3] only.
benchmark.json metadata carries placeholder model names (`executor_model` and `analyzer_model` are both '<model-name>'), so the results are not attributable to a model version.
